headline: Quantum Experts Trace 11% Productivity Decline to 1742 Plate-Meal Conundrum
deck: Hover-and-eat drones malfunction; lunch may soon require a 14-page safety filing.
article:
Dr. Marcus Hale of the National Lunch Institute pinned the 11% productivity slide on the 1742 Bread-Plate Decoherence at the Royal Society, when missing sandwiched options wrecked every subsequent midday protocol. Stacking bread slices would have broken conservation of lap momentum, a rule nobody noticed until drones started flinging hot plates into sedans at 62 mph.

Three hover-and-eat zones closed after the latest scatterings. One driver watched his casserole become road art and muttered that his lunch had just tried out for a crash-test role. Regulators now demand the 14-page filing for any plate eaten outside a strict 45-degree seated posture.

Eateries answered by carving out Seated Meal Zones and long communal tables. Patrons now trade awkward pleasantries for 45 minutes while their food cools, wondering whether the drone experiment was ever worth the paperwork.

A county official floated the idea of capping lunch-zone speeds at 15 mph so deliveries could keep plates intact and dignity semi-preserved. The suggestion landed like another drone casualty.
author: Penelope Crumble, Senior Lunchtime Correspondent

oped.title: Hats and Hazards: Defending the Sacred Safety Filing
oped.author: Dr. Archibald Cravat, Esteemed Fellow of the Bureau of Unnecessary Bureaucracy
oped.body: The 11% productivity dip has nothing to do with malfunctioning drones and everything to do with citizens dodging the 14-page safety filing. These forms, heavy on plate-balance equations and drone-arc diagrams, are the only thing standing between order and airborne casseroles. Hats are the real culprit—flimsy crowns that let quantum fields wobble. My Cravat-approved beret line, priced for the discerning bureaucrat, would lock those fields in place. Stop whining about forms and start filling them; the plates will thank you.

classifieds.text: Four hover-and-eat drones, grounded after quantum experts blamed them for the plate-meal crisis. Cash only, must pick up before the 14-page safety filing takes effect.
Office seeking Plate Holder Assistant for seated lunches; experience with anti-spill clamps required. Bonus if you can file the new federal lunch permits by Friday.
Lost during drone malfunction: one porcelain lunch plate with half-eaten quinoa. Finder must submit 14-page waiver to claim at Building C lobby.
HoverMeal Corp. apologizes for the 11% productivity drop traced to our 1742-era design flaw. All units now require pre-flight plate inspections and notarized waivers.

stories.headline: Logistics Firms Install Highway Picnic Benches After Drone Plate Drops Fall 37 Percent
stories.deck: New policy requires employees to log fork return times before clocking back in.
stories.article:
Pinnacle Logistics planted 200 concrete benches along Interstate 70 exits by its Kansas City hubs. Drivers must now pull over, eat the drone meal seated, and timestamp a receipt before wheels turn again.

The benches arrived after casseroles carpeted three lanes last month. Internal numbers expect the change to shave afternoon delays from 19 minutes down to 14.

stories.headline: State Fair Adds Plate Rental Booths Beside Every Concession Stand
stories.deck: Visitors now budget 11 extra minutes between the midway and livestock barns.
stories.article:
The Iowa State Fair rented 800 ceramic plates per food stall. Guests receive a laminated map to the nearest seated zone near the butter sculptures.

Carry-out vanished after last year’s chili spill beside the tractor pull. The 50-cent deposits are projected to pay for new signs by September.
